messages:
Maria (eng-platform): Heads-up — we need a short sync on per-model/route SLO dashboards. Proposing a single contract for metrics we need from runtime/infra teams. TL;DR: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, active_requests, queue_time, and request_rate tagged by model, route, customer_tier.

Alex (eng-runtime): +1. Do we have standard metric names? runtime currently exports latency histogram as model_infer_latency_seconds_bucket{model,route} and a gauge model_tokens_generated_total.

Samir (eng-infra): infra has node-level metrics too. For tokens/sec we prefer a rate over counter: rate(model_tokens_generated_total[1m]) per pod, then sum by (model,route).

Tanya (product): Why TTFT separate from P50? product wants TTFT as availability signal (app UX). Also want to map to per-route SLIs for canary.

Maria (eng-platform): Exactly. Suggest we define TTFT as time from request_received to first_token_emitted. Metric: model_ttft_seconds_summary{model,route,customer_tier} or a histogram. Any preference?

Alex (eng-runtime): histograms are better for percentiles in Prometheus + recording rules. Use model_ttft_seconds_bucket + exemplars from traces. We can add a label 'fallback_model' when routing falls back.

O'Brien (eng-sre): Need to ensure cardinality stays low. route and model are fine, but customer_tier might explode. Can we limit customer_tier to {free,pro,enterprise} only in ingest?

Samir (eng-infra): We can map customer_tier in the ingestion pipeline (telemetry) to those buckets. Also need guidance on cardinality for 'deployment' tag — avoid instance IDs.

Maria (eng-platform): Agreed. Also need tokens/sec and TTPS (tokens per second) as derived metrics. Proposed names: model_infer_latency_seconds_bucket, model_ttft_seconds_bucket, model_tokens_total (counter). Then compute rate(model_tokens_total[1m]) as tokens/sec.

Alex (eng-runtime): For dashboards, we want per-model rows with charts: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT P50/P95, tokens/sec with 95th percentile of throughput, and TTPS heatmap. Also include route-level quotas overlay (rate limit thresholds).

Tanya (product): Can we add a small panel showing routing policy changes (canary percent) over time? That helps explain sudden latency shifts.

Maria (eng-platform): Good call. We'll need a tag in telemetry 'routing_policy' and 'canary_percent' exported from router service. Is that feasible @alex?

Alex (eng-runtime): Router can emit routing_decision{model,route,policy,canary_percent} as a gauge; update on config change. Not expensive.

O'Brien (eng-sre): Action items: 1) runtime to add ttft histogram + exemplars (@Alex) 2) router to emit routing tags (@Alex) 3) infra to add ingestion mapping for customer_tier (@Samir) 4) product to define SLO targets per tier (@Tanya) 5) eng-platform to author dashboard templates (@Maria)

Maria (eng-platform): I'll draft the JSON schema for metric names + example PromQL and link to this thread. Plan: quick review by EOD Thu, then rollout to staging. Anyone blocking?

Samir (eng-infra): No blockers from infra side.

Alex (eng-runtime): I'll start instrumenting today, should have a PR by Wed.

Tanya (product): SLO targets: free=P95<1.2s, pro=P95<500ms, enterprise=P95<250ms. We'll refine.

O'Brien (eng-sre): Noted. I'll set up alerting playbooks once dashboards are in staging.

observability-bot: deploy:dashboard: created draft 'per-model-slo-v2' in Grafana org 'redwood' by maria — /dashboards/5321

Maria (eng-platform): Nice, thanks! :thumbsup:
